Feature: GPIO GP0 Register Reset (hreset_n) and Masked R/W Access Verification
Test Description: Validate that GPIO GP0 pin registers (GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 to GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27) power-on reset values match the documented defaults and that masked read/write operations behave correctly across these registers. For each pattern, only writable and readable bits are exercised while non-writable bits retain their reset value.
Meta Test Description: The test executes two phases over a register list defined by addr_array[] (GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8..GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27). Phase-1 (reset check): iterate i=0..CNT-1, skip if skip_rst_array[i]==1 or read_mask_array[i]==0, then data_rd = read_reg(addr_array[i]); data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe); compare data with default_value_array[i]; on mismatch increment def_fail_cnt and print failure. Phase-2 (write/read check): for each of six data patterns chk_val={0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0xf5f5f5f5,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}, write masked values to all addresses where skip_array[i]==0 and write_mask_array[i]!=0 using write_reg(addr,(data_wr & write_mask_array[i])). Then read back for each i where skip_array[i]==0, write_mask_array[i]!=0, read_mask_array[i]!=0: data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]); wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff); exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])); compare data_rd with exp_val; on mismatch increment wr_fail_cnt and print failure. At end of test_case(), if def_fail_cnt>0 || wr_fail_cnt>0 then finish(1) else finish(0). A disabled soft_reset_chk() (under #ifdef 0) shows an example soft reset sequence using SOFT_RST_REG_ADDRESS/SOFT_RST_REG_DATA but is not executed.
Remarks: Non-readable registers are skipped for reset/readback. Non-writable registers are skipped for write. During reset comparison, bit0 is masked from the read value. Input DIN bits may default high; forcing zero on DIN can alter level-select behavior and cause mismatches; avoid testing dynamic input-only fields or ensure stable external drive during validation.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the GPIO test by preparing the list of GPIO GP0 pin registers (GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 to GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27) and their documented reset values and masks.
2. For each register in the list, if it is marked readable, read its value and compare against its documented reset value while ignoring bit0; record any mismatch.
3. For each data pattern (all-ones, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000), write the pattern masked by the register’s write mask to each writable register in the list.
4. Read back each readable and writable register using the read mask and compute the expected value by combining written bits (per write mask) with the reset value for non-writable bits; compare readback with expected and record any mismatch.
5. Declare the test PASS if no mismatches were recorded in either the reset-value checks or the masked read/write checks; otherwise declare FAIL.

Test Description: Verify that enabling negative-edge interrupts for GPIO GP0 pins triggers an interrupt on a high-to-low transition, and that per-pin raw status and group status are correctly set and cleared, with system-level interrupt handling functioning as expected.
Meta Test Description: Configure SoC and platform interrupt paths for the GPIO block. Force all pads high via the pad control register at 0xA0243ffc. For each of 32 pins (offset from gp0_gpio_8 with 4-byte stride): clear any pending raw status in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1; enable the corresponding per-pin interrupt in INTR1_INTR_EN1; set an int_pend flag and create a falling edge by driving pads from high to a pattern with only the selected pin low (~(1<<i)); poll with a timeout for ISR to clear int_pend. In the ISR: clear int_pend, drive pads high, read per-pin control (gp0_gpio_8 + i*4) and check pin input low (bit0==0) and interrupt indication (bit1!=0); read group status INTR1_INTR_STS1 and ensure the pin bit is set; restore per-pin configuration; clear raw status for the pin in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1; verify INTR1_INTR_STS1 clears to zero; clear SoC-level RAW_STCR1 for the GPIO block and clear the corresponding GIC IRQ. Accumulate errors from timeouts or any verification failure and finish with pass/fail.
Remarks: Ensure the pad drive at address 0xA0243ffc reliably generates a controlled high-to-low transition on the target pin. Always clear raw interrupt status before enabling per-pin interrupts to avoid false triggers. After ISR service, confirm the group status register reads zero to prevent retrigger.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Enable the SoC interrupt for the target GPIO block and enable the corresponding platform interrupt (IRQ).
2. Drive all GPIO pads high using the pad control register to establish a known pre-edge state.
3. For each target pin: clear its raw interrupt status in the raw-status clear register and enable the pin’s interrupt in the per-group enable register.
4. Generate a falling edge on the selected pin by transitioning pads from high to a pattern with only that pin low; begin waiting for the interrupt with a timeout.
5. On interrupt, verify the pin input reads low and the group status register indicates the pin interrupt.
6. Clear the pin’s raw interrupt status and verify that the group status register clears to zero.
7. Clear the system-level raw interrupt status for the GPIO block and clear the platform IRQ.
8. Repeat for all pins and declare PASS if no timeouts or verification failures occur.

Feature: GPIO Interrupt - Positive Edge Trigger (All Pads)
Test Description: Enable positive-edge interrupts for GPIO GP0 pins (8–39). Drive pads low-to-high using the pad control at 0xA0243ffc to generate rising edges. Verify group interrupt status (INTR1_INTR_STS1) is set, clear per-pin raw status via per-pin control, confirm group status clears, and clear system-level interrupt status (RAW_STCR1) with proper IRQ handling before re-enabling interrupts.
Meta Test Description: The test sets up the platform interrupt controller for GPIO0 (IRQ 87) or GPIO1 (IRQ 88) and enables the corresponding interrupt in the LSS_SYSREG INTR_EN1 register. For each of 32 pins starting at gp0_gpio_8 (address stride 4), it programs the per-pin control with 0x00020000 to enable positive-edge detection (bit17=1). It then configures GPIO IO control groups 1–4 (pads 8–39) with 0x000000FF, waits, and enables all group interrupts by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1. For each iteration i in 0..31: the pad control at 0xA0243ffc is driven low (0x00000000), wait_on(10), then sets int_pend=1 and drives pads high (0xFFFFFFFF) to produce a rising edge. It waits for the ISR by polling int_pend with a timeout counter (2000 iterations, wait_on(10) per loop). On timeout, it logs an error and breaks. After each iteration, pads are optionally driven low again to prepare for the next edge. The Default_IRQHandler reads the group status GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, masks group interrupts by writing 0x00000000 to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, and checks that any group status is set (rdata_grp & 0xffffffff) != 0. It then clears per-pin raw status by writing 0x00010000 (iclr bit16) to each per-pin control register gp0_gpio_8 + (j*4) for j=0..31, waits, and verifies GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 reads 0x0. It clears the system-level RAW_STCR1 bit for the selected GPIO block and verifies the bit is deasserted on readback. Finally, it re-enables group interrupts by writing 0xFFFFFFFF to GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clears the corresponding GIC IRQ. The test completes with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Use the pad control register to reliably generate clean low-to-high transitions. Mask group interrupts while servicing to avoid nested interrupts. Always clear per-pin raw interrupt status before re-enabling the group and verify the group status register returns to zero to prevent retrigger. Ensure system-level interrupt status is cleared in RAW_STCR1 and the platform IRQ is cleared.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Enable the platform interrupt for the target GPIO block and enable the GPIO interrupt in the system INTR_EN1 register.
2. Configure GP0 pins (8–39) for positive-edge detection and set GPIO IO control groups 1–4 to the required input configuration.
3. Enable per-pin interrupts for the group using the INTR1_INTR_EN1 register.
4. For each pin, drive pads low, arm the wait flag, then drive pads high via the pad control to create a rising edge; wait for the ISR with a timeout.
5. In the ISR, confirm the group interrupt status shows an active bit; mask group interrupts during service.
6. Clear per-pin raw interrupt status for all pins and verify the group status register clears to zero.
7. Clear the system RAW_STCR1 bit for the GPIO block and confirm it is cleared; then re-enable group interrupts and clear the platform IRQ.
8. Repeat for all pins and pass if no timeouts or verification failures occur.
